text:
eli: Heads up — after the kernel selector change deployed to canary, we've seen a spike in OOMs on p4d when batches include long-chat requests. Not just token budget — KV cache footprint seems to be the culprit. Profiling attached.

maya: ah — that makes sense. Kernel change reduces per-token mem a bit but increases KV allocation for long contexts? any concrete numbers? :thinking_face:

eli: short profile snippet:
```
allocations: model_state 120MB, kv_cache 2.4GB, activation 900MB
batch tokens: 5200
```
KV allocation jumps when we pick the new 'fast_attn' kernel for contexts > 8k.

chris: are admission heuristics using only estimated token counts? iirc admission checks token_budget and slot_limit but not kv bytes. that would explain misses.

maya: right now admission = token_budget && slot_limit. we experimented with a naive kv check in staging but throughput tanked for some workloads. need smarter heuristic.

eli: Proposal (high level): add a per-device soft_kv_budget (e.g., 75% of free kv memory) and enforce both token_budget and kv_budget during batch formation. Also make kv_per_token an adaptive estimate from recent seq_len histogram. Pseudocode:
```
kv_per_token = model_config.kv_bytes_per_token
est_kv = req.seq_len * kv_per_token
if batch.kv_sum + est_kv > device.kv_soft_limit: reject
elif batch.tokens + req.tokens > token_budget: reject
else accept
```

zane: +1. Also add slow, conservative backoff: if reject_rate_over_window > 0.1 then reduce soft_kv_limit by 15% and widen the latency SLO for queued requests. avoids oscillation between full/empty.

chris: what about queue reordering to prefer short seq_len when kv pressure is high? that should reclaim headroom without sacrificing throughput for small requests.

maya: we discussed priority reordering. lightweight heuristic: when kv_pressure_flag is set, sort queue by estimated_kv_bytes/token_ratio (lowest first). small CPU cost, big win for tail OOMs.

deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled: 2026-01-12 03:00 UTC -> 10% of p4d clusters.

eli: plan: implement kv_budget + queue reordering + dynamic soft_limit adjustments behind a feature flag. run perf tests with representative chat traces tomorrow (mix of short/long contexts). need dashboards: kv_alloc_gauge, batch_kv_hist, accept_reject_breakdown, per-device oom_rate.

chris: I'll own the dashboard. also add regression alert: oom_rate_per_hour > 0.5 triggers page + auto-rollback.

maya: I'll start the PR for admission changes and include a small replay test harness. tagging @chris for dashboards and @zane for the backoff logic.

eli: Sweet. Let's aim for a staging canary by EOD and perf run overnight. Thanks all.
